transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood. We'll kick off \u2014 Priya and Marco are with me on the SE side. Kai, Lena, Samir, Rae on Aurelius side?

[00:14] Kai Morgan: Yeah that's right, thanks. We've been looking at Redwood's Private offering and want a deep dive into networking and runtime performance implications. Long story short: low latency, predictable throughput, and no data egress where possible.

[00:28] Priya Raman: Great, we'll cover PrivateLink vs peering, NAT/egress, DNS, and then walk through runtime considerations \u2014 KV cache locality, batching, quantization tradeoffs. Sound good?

[00:38] Rae Chen: Yes. Quick context: we're running in us-east-1 across three AZs. VPCs are /16, we use NAT gateways in each AZ, and we have an internal transit setup to connect some legacy on-prem via Direct Connect. We also have strict egress cost concerns.

[00:56] Marco Silva: Understood. For Redwood Private we typically provide two connectivity patterns: 1) PrivateLink endpoints from your VPC to our service endpoints (recommended for minimal routing changes), or 2) VPC peering / Transit Gateway for dedicated network paths. Each has pros/cons.

[01:12] Lena Ortiz: Can you clarify control-plane traffic? We don't want keys or payloads traversing public internet even for control plane calls.

[01:20] Priya Raman: Absolutely. With PrivateLink, the control plane sits behind an interface endpoint in your VPC \u2014 traffic goes over AWS network, stays within AZ for the ENI, and you don't need NAT for those flows. With peering or TGW you can route directly but you manage the routing. PrivateLink also simplifies DNS with endpoint-specific hostnames.

[01:42] Samir Patel: What about S3/ECR access? Our deployment will pull model artifacts and maybe container images from S3/ECR \u2014 do we need special endpoints?

[01:50] Jordan Lee: Good call. You can use VPC endpoints for S3 and ECR, or S3 Gateway endpoints. For ECR we recommend private links or endpoint policies. Also if you're using our curated models that are hosted in a storage account, we'll provide the exact endpoints and recommend locking them down with endpoint policies.

[02:08] Rae Chen: How do NAT gateways affect token throughput? We worry about NAT scaling and SNAT port exhaustion with many concurrent connections during model pulls or control-plane bursts.

[02:18] Priya Raman: NAT gateways don't meaningfully affect per-token generation \u2014 runtime traffic is mostly long-lived TLS connections to the dedicated runtime shards. However, initial model pulls and control plane calls are short-lived and can spike. For large-scale model pulls we advise using S3 VPC endpoints so you don't hit NAT and to pre-warm caches.

[02:36] Kai Morgan: We also plan to run inference inside our VPC \u2014 Redwood nodes will be in our subnets, right? How does that work for on-prem/private?

[02:44] Marco Silva: For Private deployments we offer two modes: 1) Redwood-managed nodes in your VPC (we deploy agent nodes that attach to your subnets and report to a private control plane), or 2) fully customer-managed on-prem where you run the runtime and only the control plane talks back to Redwood. The former is typical and requires specific subnet ranges and outbound connectivity for control-plane health checks and telemetry.

[03:06] Rae Chen: Outbound \u2014 is that over PrivateLink too? We need to know exactly which FQDNs/IPs must be reachable.

[03:12] Priya Raman: We'll provide a list. With PrivateLink, control-plane flows are via interface endpoints so you can lock it down. If you do egress to our control plane over the public network, we'll provide IP ranges but PrivateLink is cleaner.

[03:26] Jordan Lee: Also note the control plane uses mTLS and mutual auth \u2014 we exchange certs and you can optionally require customer mTLS for agent registration.

[03:36] Samir Patel: For KMS: can we use our KMS (CMK) to wrap model keys and logs? HSM?

[03:42] Priya Raman: Yes \u2014 we support KMS integration. For fully private/on-prem deployments you can bring your own KMS or HSM and we can configure the runtime to decrypt locally. We'll share the KMS integration docs. There are a few caveats around key access patterns and bootstrap \u2014 we'll include those.

[03:58] Kai Morgan: Switching to runtime \u2014 we're very concerned about p95/p99 latency at 1\u20132k QPS with mixed prompt lengths. How does KV cache and batching impact latency if traffic is split across AZs?

[04:12] Marco Silva: Great question. KV cache locality is critical. If the runtime shard serving a session has a hot KV cache in the same AZ, you'll get minimal overhead. If cache misses cause remote KV fetching across AZs or across the network to a central cache, you'll see higher p99s. Our recommendation is to colocate runtime shards with the model KV cache in the same subnet/AZ and use load balancing that respects session affinity.

[04:36] Rae Chen: Session affinity \u2014 do you mean sticky LB or pinning at application layer?

[04:40] Priya Raman: Both ways work. We have session-pin options where the orchestration pins a session to a shard; alternatively, you can configure your LB to keep sticky sessions. Sticky at LB level can cause imbalance under churn, so orchestration pinning tends to be more robust for long-lived chat sessions.

[04:58] Lena Ortiz: What about batching? We prefer batching to reduce GPU cost, but we can't have high tail latency. How do you balance that?

[05:06] Marco Silva: We use dynamic batching with latency SLOs. The runtime will form micro-batches for tokens while respecting per-request latency budgets. You can configure a target latency window (e.g., 50ms max batching delay) and it will flush if the budget is near. For workloads with spiky short requests, we recommend shorter batching windows and more instances to keep p99 low.

[05:26] Kai Morgan: Quantization \u2014 if we use int8/4-bit variants, how much perf gain vs quality drop should we expect? Also does that change networking?

[05:34] Priya Raman: Quantization reduces GPU memory footprint and can increase throughput (tokens/sec) substantially, sometimes 1.5-3x depending on model and quantization scheme. Quality delta varies by model \u2014 we recommend running evals. Networking-wise, quantization can reduce the need to shard KV across nodes because more of the model can fit on a single GPU, which improves locality and reduces cross-node traffic.

[05:56] Rae Chen: Are there any port ranges or protocols we need to open between subnets for inter-node communication?

[06:02] Marco Silva: The runtime uses gRPC over TLS for inter-node comms. We'll provide the specific ports (typically a small range, e.g., 10000-10010) but you can restrict by security group rules. For high throughput we recommend enhanced ENI settings and making sure your subnets are sized to avoid IP shortages.

[06:18] Lena Ortiz: ENI limits \u2014 we operate on c5n and m6i families with bursty traffic. Any guidance on instance types and network bandwidth per instance?

[06:26] Priya Raman: For best results with our runtime, GPU instance types with high PCIe/NIC bandwidth (A100/H100 on supported clouds) are preferred. On AWS, instance ENI bandwidth and maximum packets-per-second can affect throughput; we can share recommended families and expected tokens/sec baselines.

[06:44] Kai Morgan: DNS \u2014 split-horizon is our model. PrivateLink will give hostnames that resolve to the endpoint; how do you handle internal DNS and certificate validation?

[06:52] Jordan Lee: We recommend setting up conditional forwarding so your internal resolver resolves the Redwood service name to the interface endpoint IP. Our certs are valid for the service hostnames we provide, so as long as DNS resolves to the endpoint IPs, TLS will validate. If you have mTLS we exchange certs at the handshake.

[07:12] Samir Patel: For audit logs, do you push logs back to our S3 or do you keep them in your system with export hooks? We need full audit trail for model inputs/outputs metadata.

[07:22] Priya Raman: We can do both: we store audit logs centrally with retention controls and provide an export connector to push logs to your S3 via a VPC endpoint. For air-gapped setups, we can deploy a local log forwarder that writes to your internal storage.

[07:36] Rae Chen: Performance tests \u2014 what do you need from us to run the benchmark?

[07:40] Marco Silva: We'll need CIDR ranges for worker subnets, expected QPS and prompt distribution, sample prompts and input sizes, and a target latency SLO. We'll run a preliminary benchmark from our side and then do an in-VPC run during a scheduled window. We'll provide metrics and traces (token-level timing).

[07:58] Kai Morgan: There's also a cost question: PrivateLink per-ENI costs and data processing charges vs TGW transit costs. Can you help model that?

[08:06] Jordan Lee: Yes we'll include a cost comparison worksheet in the checklist. For sustained high egress, TGW or peering can be cheaper; for security and simplicity PrivateLink often wins.

[08:18] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas about NACLs? We use strict NACLs across subnets and occasionally block ephemeral ports.

[08:24] Priya Raman: NACLs are stateless, so if you restrict ephemeral ports you might break gRPC connections which use ephemeral ports for responses. Security groups are stateful and preferred for node-to-node rules. We'll include recommended SG and NACL settings.

[08:42] Kai Morgan: Ok that's a lot. Quick recap?

[08:46] Jordan Lee: Recap: 1) We'll send the Private VPC checklist with required endpoints, ports (gRPC/TLS), and DNS recommendations. 2) Priya will send a perf benchmark plan and load scripts. 3) Aurelius will share VPC CIDRs, NAT details, route tables, and expected QPS. 4) Security will review KMS/HSM docs. 5) Schedule a 2-hour in-VPC benchmark next week if possible.

[09:12] Samir Patel: Sounds good. One more: if we see p99 spikes during bursts, what's your standard mitigation?

[09:18] Marco Silva: Typical mitigations: increase shard count to reduce per-shard load, reduce batching windows, pre-warm KV caches by routing warmed sessions to the right shards, and fallback to a lower-cost model variant if latency is critical. We'll also instrument to see if spikes are due to cross-AZ traffic or GPU stalls.

[09:36] Rae Chen: Please send the doc with exact ports and hostnames. That will help our firewall team.

[09:42] Jordan Lee: Will do. We'll also attach a sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet for the PrivateLink interface endpoint and recommended endpoint policies.

[09:52] Kai Morgan: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the VPC details to you tomorrow.

[09:56] Jordan Lee: Great \u2014 thanks. We'll follow up with the checklist and perf plan.

[10:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (product names sometimes transcribed as Red wood). References to exact port ranges and IP lists will be attached in the checklist artifact.
